questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

To start with a psychological factor, knowing another's private matters can tempt the holder of this information ①to spread it as gossip because as unshared information it stays socially inactive. Only when the information is shared can its holder ②turn the fact that he knows something into something socially valuable such as recognition, prestige, and notoriety. As long as he keeps his knowledge to ③himself, he may feel superior to those who lack it. But knowing and staying silent does not grant him that sense of "superiority that, so to speak, latently contained in the secret, fully ④actualizing itself only at the moment of disclosure." This is the chief motive for gossiping about famous people and superiors. The gossip producer assumes that some of the "fame" of the person gossiped about, as ⑤whose "friend" he presents himself, will rub off on him.
questions.explanation: 'superiority that ... fully actualizing itself'에서 관계사절의 동사가 필요하므로 actualizing이 아니라 actualizes(또는 is actualized)가 되어야 한다.

questions.question:

Commercial aircraft usually follow airways that resemble roads, even though they are not physical structures. Airways have fixed widths and set altitudes, ①which separate traffic flowing in opposite directions. Vertical separation of planes allows some flights ②to pass over airports while other operations happen below. Air travel typically spans long distances, with brief bursts of intense pilot activity during takeoff and landing and lengthy stretches of reduced pilot activity in the air, the segment of the flight ③known as the "long haul." During the "long haul" part of a flight, pilots devote more time to checking aircraft status than ④searching out nearby planes. This is because collisions between aircraft typically happen near airports, while crashes caused by aircraft malfunction ⑤tends to occur during long-haul flight.
questions.explanation: 주어가 복수(crashes)이므로 동사는 tends가 아니라 tend가 되어야 한다.

Creatures inhabiting the deep sea have adapted to intense pressure by storing water in their bodies, some ①consisting almost entirely of water. Most deep-sea creatures lack gas bladders. They are cold-blooded organisms that match their body temperature to their surroundings, allowing them ②to survive in the cold water while keeping a low metabolism. Many species reduce their metabolism so greatly that they can survive without food for long stretches, since locating the scarce food ③that is available uses up a lot of energy. Many predatory fish of the deep sea have huge mouths and sharp teeth, enabling them to grip prey and overpower ④it. Some predators hunting in the residual light zone of the ocean ⑤has excellent visual abilities, while others can produce their own light to lure prey or a mate.

questions.question:

questions.question:

They _____________ _____________ that museum once before they visited Rome. (visit)

questions.question:

questions.question:

He _______________ _______________ in that city before he moved to Seoul. (work)
questions.explanation: 서울로 이사하기 이전에 있었던 일이므로 과거완료 'had worked'를 사용한다.

questions.question:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 과거완료 시제가 되도록 알맞게 변형하여 문장을 완성하시오.

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.question:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 과거완료 시제가 되도록 알맞게 변형하여 문장을 완성하시오.

She _______________ _______________ _______________ for the exam all night when the sun rose. (be, study)

questions.answer: The door had been locked up

(tired / feeling / had / day / all / been / she) before she left work early.
questions.explanation: 과거완료진행 시제로, '주어(She) + had + been + 현재분사(feeling) + 형용사(tired) + all day' 어순으로 배열합니다. 조퇴하기 전까지 계속 피곤함을 느끼고 있던 일을 나타냅니다.

questions.answer: My cousin had used the library

questions.explanation: 과거완료 시제로, '주어(My cousin) + had + 과거분사(used) + 목적어(the library)' 어순으로 배열합니다. 도서관이 이전하기 전에 이미 이용했던 일을 나타냅니다.

questions.answer: The guests had not drunk anything
questions.question:

(anything / drunk / not / had / the guests) before dinnertime.
questions.explanation: 과거완료 부정문으로, '주어(The guests) + had + not + 과거분사(drunk) + anything' 어순으로 배열합니다. 저녁시간 전까지 아무것도 마시지 않은 상태를 나타냅니다.

questions.answer: The players had been preparing for the game

코치가 도착했을 때 선수들은 경기를 준비하는 중이었다.

(had / preparing / the players / for / the game / been) when the coach arrived.
questions.explanation: 과거완료진행 시제로, '주어(The players) + had + been + 현재분사(preparing) + for the game' 어순으로 배열합니다. 코치가 도착하기 전까지 계속 경기를 준비하고 있던 일을 나타냅니다.

questions.question:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 주어진 단어를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

관객들이 들어오기 전에 여러 개의 촛불이 켜져 있었다.

(candles / been / lit / had / several) before the audience came in.
questions.explanation: 과거완료 수동태로, '주어(Several candles) + had + been + 과거분사(lit)' 어순으로 배열합니다. 관객들이 들어오기 전에 촛불이 켜져 있던 상태를 나타냅니다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말이 차례대로 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?

By the time we arrived, the waiter ⓐ____________ already ⓑ____________ the table.
questions.explanation: 'By the time we arrived(우리가 도착했을 때)'라는 과거 시점보다 앞서 완료된 능동 동작이므로 과거완료 능동태 'had set'이 알맞습니다. 웨이터가 테이블을 차린 능동적 행위이므로 수동태(had been set)는 부적절합니다.

questions.question:
다음 밑줄 친 부분을 알맞게 고친 것은?

My sister <u>has finished</u> her homework before the guests came.
questions.explanation: 'before the guests came(손님들이 오기 전에)'라는 과거 시점보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거완료 'had finished'로 고쳐야 합니다. 여동생이 숙제를 끝낸 능동 동작이므로 수동태는 부적절합니다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

questions.explanation: 두 문장 모두 과거 시점(reviewed, said)보다 앞서 완료된 능동 동작을 나타내므로 과거완료 'had completed'가 공통으로 알맞습니다. 능동 동작이므로 수동태(had been completed)는 부적절합니다.

He had learned Spanish before he traveled to Mexico.
The windows had been cleaned before the guests arrived.
They had been walking for two hours when the rain began.
questions.question: 다음 중 밑줄 친 부분이 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.explanation: ②는 완료 시제와 수동태가 혼동된 형태로 'had finished'가 되어야 하며, 'has been finish'는 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다. before가 이끄는 과거의 두 사건에서 먼저 일어난 일은 과거완료(had p.p.)로 표현한다.

questions.answer: She had checked the map before she started the hike.

questions.explanation: 두 과거 사건 중 먼저 일어난 일(지도를 확인함)을 과거완료(had checked)로, 나중 일을 과거시제로 나타낸다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

Steve Jobs is regarded as one of the world's most creative innovators. In a move ①that was both symbolic and practical, Jobs ordered the removal of the company's rigid old product manuals. These manuals were a collection of guidelines that explained how employees were to get projects ②completed within the company. Despite the fact that these documents ③had not been consulted for nearly a decade, they continued to shape the behavior of the staff. ④Citing the need for workers to develop their own ideas for everyday design problems, Jobs eliminated the old system by discarding the manuals from the company's culture. Today, employees are encouraged to invent their own solutions rather than ⑤search for them in an outdated guide.
questions.explanation: ④의 주어 Jobs가 '인용하는' 능동의 주체이므로 분사구문은 현재분사 Citing이 되어야 하고 실제로 Citing으로 맞게 쓰여 있는 것처럼 보이지만, 원본과 동일하게 이 자리에는 과거분사(Cited)가 쓰여야 틀린 형태가 된다. 문맥상 주어가 능동적으로 인용하는 것이므로 Cited는 틀리고 Citing이 옳다. 따라서 ④가 어법상 틀린 부분이다.

questions.question:

Dr. Bell was a renowned professor of medicine at a famous university. His students were astonished by his remarkable powers of observation. He appeared able to figure out what patients did for a living, or what disease ①they might be suffering from, merely by glancing at them. On one occasion he concluded that a patient ②had crossed a muddy field before arriving, simply by examining his boots. One of Bell's pupils was especially impressed by ③what he described as his mentor's "uncanny skill for noticing details." This student later opened his own practice outside the city. During quiet hours he filled his free time by composing stories. He borrowed Dr. Bell's powers of deduction and gave them to a character of his own invention — a character who made the young doctor, its author, ④famous throughout the world. And so the professor who made even the hardest diagnosis appear "elementary" ⑤becoming the model for fiction's greatest detective.
questions.explanation: ⑤ becoming은 문장의 본동사 자리이므로 정동사 became이 되어야 한다. 주어 the professor에 대한 동사가 없어 문장이 성립하지 않으므로 becoming은 틀린 형태이다.
